title: The ruling party demanded that the Congress publicly apologise within 24 hours for the "insult" to the national song
author: PTI
content_html:
The BJP on Sunday (August 16, 2026) alleged that opposing anything patriotic is the Congress' policy and asked if anyone believing in the sovereignty and integrity of India would get "angry" over the invocation of Vande Mataram on Independence Day.

The ruling party demanded that the Congress publicly apologise within 24 hours for the "insult" to the national song if it has even an "iota" of patriotism.

The remarks came in the wake of the BJP's allegations that Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge showed "utter disrespect" towards Vande Mataram when it was sung at the party's Independence Day event on Friday (August 14).

The Congress denied the allegation, asserting that there was no attempt to stop the singing of the full version of the national song and that Sonia Gandhi was only asking for a chair for party chief Mallikarjun Kharge as he had been standing for some time.

Addressing a press conference here, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said the Opposition to Vande Mataram by Rahul and Sonia Gandhi on Independence Day points towards a mindset of a "dimagi Naxal ecosystem".

"Can any patriot, can any Indian who believes in the Constitution of India, respects the Tricolour of India, respects India's freedom fighters and believes in India's sovereignty and integrity, ever get angry at the invocation of Vande Mataram on Independence Day?" he said.

"The Congress has not only insulted the freedom fighters but also the Constitution of this country, its sovereignty and integrity, and the 140 crore people of this country," Mr. Bhandari said.

The "dimagi Naxal" reference came from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day address to the nation, in which he warned against "dimagi Naxals" who have entrenched themselves in the system and urged people to identify and isolate them.

Accusations against Congress

Flag hoisting by Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge with Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and former president of AICC, Sonia Gandhi | Photo Credit: The Hindu

He alleged that Sonia Gandhi gestured to stop the singing of Vande Mataram at the Congress headquarters and later expressed her anger when it continued.

"If you look carefully at the video, when Vande Mataram is being invoked at the Congress Party headquarters, Sonia Gandhi indicates with her hand that they should stop. She gestures that Vande Mataram should be stopped at the Congress Party headquarters.”

"When she is not listened to, she again gestures for the second time and says that it must be stopped." Mr. Bhandari claimed Rahul Gandhi could be heard saying, "We don't need to sing Vande Mataram" after its rendition was completed and played a purported audio clip before the media.

The BJP spokesperson said Sonia and Rahul Gandhi should apologise within 24 hours to every patriotic Indian who is "deeply angry and enraged" by the Congress' conduct.

He alleged that the Congress' Opposition to Vande Mataram is part of its policy of opposing anything patriotic and questioned whether Rahul Gandhi is fit to be the Leader of Opposition.

"Any leader of Opposition who considers the Parliament of this country supreme can never insult the national song," Mr. Bhandari said.

He also alleged that the Congress government in Kerala skipped Vande Mataram at an official event, saying this shows that the party's conduct at its headquarters is not an isolated incident.

Mr. Bhandari also attacked senior Congress leader P. Chidambaram over his response to Modi's "dimagi Naxal' remark. Chidambaram on Sunday (August 16) said he is proud to be a 'dimagi Naxal'.

"And this country's Gen Z and youth are Gen P, Gen Patriotic, Gen Nationalist. They know that on Independence Day, when 140 crore Indians are holding the tricolour, celebrating with happiness and pride and taking the resolve of Viksit Bharat 2047 under Prime Minister Modi's leadership, only the Gandhi-Vadra family, only Rahul Gandhi and Sonia Gandhi in the Congress ecosystem, have a problem," he added.

title: ONGC gets U.S. licence to resume full Venezuela operations, eyes operatorship
author: PTI
content_html:
State-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) has secured a licence from the U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), allowing it to resume full operations in Venezuela after years of limiting activity because of sanctions-related risks, a senior company official said.

The U.S. approval removes a key hurdle for ONGC's Venezuelan investments and could pave the way for the state-run explorer to expand production, sign new agreements and take over operatorship of some projects from Venezuela's state oil company PDVSA, Anupam Agarwal, director-finance at ONGC, said at an investor call post first quarter earnings announcement.

"Now we have full freedom to work on the Venezuela project because earlier we were restricting our operations there because of the sanction-related risks. Those risks are behind us," Mr. Agarwal said.

ONGC Videsh Ltd, the company's overseas investment arm, holds a 40% interest in the San Cristobal oil project, while the remaining is with Venezuela's Petroleos de Venezuela S.A. (PDVSA).

It holds another 11% stake in the Carabobo project, which is under development.

An OFAC license would enable the company to manage the finances of its Venezuelan projects and help it recover a pending dividend of more than $500 million.

ONGC is already in talks with Venezuelan authorities and its joint-venture partners over its interests in two projects, San Cristobal and Carabobo, and expects positive developments soon, including new agreements and a possible transfer of operatorship from PDVSA, he said.

The licence is significant for ONGC because U.S. sanctions on Venezuela's oil sector have for years complicated financial transactions, investment and operations involving Venezuelan crude and energy assets. The company had therefore curtailed activity despite its longstanding presence in the country.

The company can now invest in the projects to raise oil production. San Cristobal produced around 0.265 million tonnes of oil equivalent in FY26. This is a 10th of the production potential, and the OFAC license means it can invest in raising output.

Venezuela’s strategic importance

Venezuela is strategically important for ONGC because it holds the world's largest proven crude oil reserves, estimated by OPEC at about 303 billion barrels, more than Saudi Arabia. Much of the country's production potential remains constrained by years of underinvestment, sanctions and operational difficulties, leaving substantial scope for additional development.

Mr. Agarwal said Venezuela's newly enacted petroleum law provides additional fiscal incentives for resource development, potentially improving the investment environment for foreign oil companies and their local partners.

“ONGC's focus is on shallow, onshore fields in Venezuela, where it has relevant operating expertise from its domestic fields in Western India, including Mehsana and Ahmedabad,” Mr. Agarwal said.

The company sees the projects as a natural fit with its existing capabilities and is now seeking to accelerate development after the easing of sanctions-related constraints.

"We are very bullish for Venezuela," Mr. Agarwal said, adding that ONGC expects to see new agreements and potentially take over operatorship of some projects from PDVSA in the near term.

OVL invested in Venezuelan oil assets through joint ventures, but sanctions imposed by Washington on Venezuela's oil sector have periodically restricted the scope of operations and dealings with PDVSA.

The renewed push into Venezuela comes as India seeks to secure overseas oil resources and diversify its supply base amid heightened geopolitical risks.

For ONGC, greater operational control over Venezuelan fields could also give the company a larger role in unlocking some of the world's biggest undeveloped and underproduced hydrocarbon resources.

title: Rahul lauds courage of India's youth for standing firm against 'Modi's violent regime'
author: PTI
content_html:
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday (August 16, 2026) said the courage with which India's youngsters have stood firm against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "violent regime" is commendable, as he lauded the girls who faced "misbehavior, verbal abuse and violence" at the hands of "BJP goons".

Mr. Gandhi shared on social media a video of his interaction with students who had protested last month seeking then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the issue of paper leaks and faced alleged police excesses on July 20.

Mr. Gandhi heard the students' experiences of police "brutality" and "harassment" that followed after they raised their voice.

The interaction between Mr. Gandhi and the students took place earlier this month.

In a post in Hindi along with the video, Mr. Gandhi said, "The courage and resilience with which India's youngsters have stood firm against Modiji's violent regime, demanding accountability, is commendable." They raised their voice with peace, love and humour, the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha said.

"I am proud of every single young person — especially the girls who faced the BJP goons' misbehaviour, verbal abuse and violence, even being forced to apologise to the Prime Minister," Mr. Gandhi said.

But now, their voices cannot be silenced, he asserted.

On August 22, "Chhatron ki Goonj", an event where he interacts with students, is arriving in Pune and this time, it will be exclusively for girls, Gandhi said.

"Now, the girls will speak and the country will listen," the Congress leader added.

भारत के युवाओं ने मोदी जी के हिंसक शासन के सामने जिस साहस और मजबूती से खड़े होकर जवाबदेही की मांग की, वह काबिल-ए-तारीफ है।

उन्होंने शांति, मोहब्बत और हंसी-मज़ाक के साथ अपनी आवाज़ बुलंद की।

मुझे हर एक युवा पर गर्व है - खासकर उन लड़कियों पर, जिन्हें BJP के गुंडों की बदसलूकी,… pic.twitter.com/JOVCj4WCkd

— Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) August 16, 2026

Mr. Gandhi had addressed a press conference after meeting the students on August 5. The five students with whom he had appeared before the media included model Rhiya Ahir, whose picture blocking a police van during student protests in Mumbai had gone viral. She has approached police alleging online harassment.

title: Raut defends Rahul over his remarks against Amit Shah
author: PTI
content_html:
Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut on Sunday (August 16, 2026) invoked the title of a popular Bollywood movie to defend Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi's remarks against Union Home Minister Amit Shah, saying they can't be construed as "unparliamentary".

The Lok Sabha secretariat has sought a response from Mr. Gandhi to two separate complaints of "breach of privilege" filed by BJP MPs Anurag Thakur and Sanjay Jaiswal for his remarks against Mr. Shah during a debate on the anti-paper leak bill. The secretariat has asked Mr. Gandhi to submit his response to the allegations against him by August 28.

"Idiot is not an unparliamentary word. Calling anyone silly is not unparliamentary. The usage of the word hurts those who are silly. It's government silliness if Gandhi has been issued any notice," Mr. Raut told reporters.

Recalling Bollywood blockbuster "3 Idiots", which had received a national award, the Rajya Sabha member argued that if “idiot” is an unparliamentary word, then the Censor Board should be banned.

Mr. Raut alleged the Union Home Minister does not come to Parliament and answer questions.

"All idiots are being brought together, and the governments are being run in Maharashtra and the country," he alleged.

On Yoga guru Ramdev reportedly warning of a potential new protest over alleged corruption in education and recruitment examinations, Mr. Raut said the former seems to have realised the changing direction of political winds in the country.

"Ramdev seems to have realised that the current government will change. He knows about possible raids by Central agencies after the government is changed and is exercising caution," Mr. Raut claimed.

title: ‘Propitious environment needs to be created’: Bangladesh says PM Tarique Rahman will not visit India until Hasina’s extradition
author: Kallol Bhattacherjee
content_html:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) in Dhaka said on Sunday (August 16, 2026) that officials of India and Bangladesh have been in talks for “several weeks” for a possible India visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and stated that the atmosphere of bilateral relations was “vitiated” by deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s August 5, 2026, press conference held in Delhi’s Foreign Correspondents Club.

MoFA’s official spokesperson A.K.M. Shahidul Karim said that “a propitious environment” is required for Mr. Rahman’s visit and urged India to “extradite” Ms. Hasina and the suspected killers of radical student leader Osman Hadi.

“We are of the view that a propitious environment needs to be created for the visit. To this end, we have requested the Indian authorities to expeditiously act on our request to extradite Sheikh Hasina and other fugitive criminals, and to hand over to Bangladesh the accused killers of Shaheed Sharif Osman Hadi in compliance with our bilateral extradition treaty,” said Mr. Karim in a statement, adding, “We are awaiting their response.”

Ms. Hasina sought refuge in India on August 5, 2024, after a popular uprising toppled her government. Hadi, a radical student leader who was part of the protests and subsequently planned to contest the election, was shot in Dhaka by unknown assailants in December 2025. He passed away in Singapore while undergoing treatment on December 18, 2025, leading to widespread violence in Bangladesh some of which also targeted India’s diplomatic missions and minority Hindu community members. Dhaka has been maintaining that the suspected shooters involved in the incident escaped to India, but New Delhi has not said anything definitive in response.

Diplomatic sources had earlier indicated that bilateral talks had been on the right track after India distanced itself from Ms. Hasina’s press conference in which she had targeted Mr. Rahman’s government. Subsequently, Indian High Commissioner to Dhaka Dinesh Trivedi called on Mr. Rahman on August 10.

In view of these exchanges, sources in Dhaka had indicated that “positive movements” had started and that the window for a big ticket visit from Dhaka was gradually opening. Mr. Karim confirmed the consultation and said, “Officials of Bangladesh and Inda have been in touch with each other for several weeks on the possibility of a bilateral visit by Honourable Prime Minister Mr. Tarique Rahman to India. However, this process was vitiated by the open press interaction in New Delhi on August 5 by Sheikh Hasina…”.

The official spokesperson of the External Affairs Ministry, Randhir Jaiswal, had reiterated last Friday that India had extended two invites to Prime Minister Rahman – one for the upcoming BRICS summit to be held here and the other an invite for a bilateral visit. The latter was extended on February 17, when Mr. Rahman was sworn in after winning the general election. Earlier, on August 7, Mr. Jaiswal had distanced India from Ms. Hasina’s press conference saying that India does not “endorse” the comments made against the “duly constituted government” of Bangladesh.

In Sunday’s remarks, Mr. Karim reiterated Dhaka’s “Bangladesh first” foreign policy and said the government will continue to “promote friendly bilateral relations with other countries” including with neighbours, “on the basis of sovereign equality, national dignity, non-interference in each other’s internal affairs and mutual benefit”.

title: Congress should apologise for insulting Vande Mataram on Independence Day: Amit Shah
author: PTI
content_html:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday (August 16, 2026) accused the Congress of insulting the national song 'Vande Mataram' and demanded that the party apologise to the people and to Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay who wrote the song.

Addressing a public meeting in Chittorgarh, Mr. Shah alleged that during the Independence Day programme at the Congress headquarters, party leader Sonia Gandhi asked Vande Mataram to be stopped midway through the song.

The Home Minister alleged that the Congress had forgotten Vande Mataram due to vote-bank politics.

Referring to the Independence Day celebrations held on Saturday (August 15, 2026), Mr. Shah said that after 80 years of Independence, Vande Mataram was sung at the Red Fort and at all other places where flag hoisting was held.

"Thousands of people faced bullets and lathis and were jailed for singing Vande Mataram," Mr. Shah said, referring to the use of the revolutionary slogan during the freedom struggle.

He alleged that during the Independence Day programme at the Congress headquarters, Sonia Gandhi had asked the party president to stop the song midway.

"We all saw it on television," Mr. Shah said, adding that Sonia Gandhi should apologise to the people and to Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's immortal soul.

"If there is any shame left, you should fold your hands and apologise to Bankim Babu's immortal spirit and the people," he said.

Addressing the gathering at 'Atal Gaurav Smriti Samaroh' held on the death anniversary of Atal Bihari Vajpayee, Mr. Shah highlighted the contributions of the former Prime Minister.

Vajpayee took several major decisions, including making India a nuclear power despite international pressure after the Pokhran tests, Mr. Shah said.

He said Vajpayee's government connected villages with roads, built national highways and launched several initiatives during its tenure. He also credited Vajpayee with establishing a separate ministry for tribal development.

The Home Minister said the progress made in tribal welfare was reflected in the election of Droupadi Murmu as President of India, who came from a tribal family and rose to the top post.

He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has continued to give priority to tribal welfare.

Earlier, Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma said the country's borders were becoming safer under Mr. Shah's leadership and Rajasthan was also benefiting from it.

Mr. Sharma said the State was progressing under the guidance of Prime Minister Modi and credited Mr. Shah with playing an important role in eliminating the problem of Left-wing extremism and implementing new criminal laws.

Published - August 16, 2026 02:45 pm IST

title: Veteran Malayalam actor Devan quits BJP, accuses party’s State unit of giving social reformer Sree Narayana Guru’s ideals the go-by
author: G Anand
content_html:
Veteran Malayalam film actor Devan on Sunday publicly aired his intention to quit the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), accusing the State unit of veering away from the ideals of social reformer and renaissance leader Sree Narayana Guru.

Notably, Mr. Devan, who is currently the BJP’s State vice-president, made his “resolve” clear at a function at the Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam-controlled Kanichukulangara Devi temple in Alappuzha. SNDP Yogam general secretary Vellapally Natesan heads the temple’s administrative committee. 

Mr. Devan said the BJP had veered away from the progressive social justice agenda set by the social reformer. “My politics is based on the social ideals of Guru. In the past five years, I have not seen them reflected in the BJP in Kerala. I have realised that the BJP State unit’s current line does not agree with my political orientation guided by the Guru’s ideals,” he added. 

‘Contributed to poll win’

Mr. Devan claimed that as the vice-president, he had pursued his organisational and political responsibilities with vigour and passion. “I worked aggressively for the BJP. I contributed to the victory of BJP’s candidates, including the party’s State president Rajeev Chandrasekhar in the 2026 Assembly elections. Even Mr. Chandrasekhar cannot deny the fact,” he added.

Mr. Devan said he arrived at his decision to quit the BJP’s primary membership after much introspection. “I had decided to part ways with the BJP in early 2026. I waited to make the declaration pointedly at the Kanichukulangara temple,” he said. 

Series of controversies

Mr. Devan forayed into politics from the tinsel world in 2004. He launched the Kerala Peoples Party, which he merged with the BJP in 2021 at the instance of Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Mr. Devan’s resignation from the BJP comes as the party’s State unit confronts a series of controversies, including alleged diversion of Assembly election funds for private use, leadership absenteeism, impaired political orientation and response and “factionalism.”

Mr. Chandrasekhar has repeatedly denied the accusations. BJP leader P.C. George had raised the election fund misuse allegation, which he later sought to retract on Sunday. The Centre’s recent amendment to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act has threatened BJP’s social engineering outreach to Kerala’s Christian community and backwards-class voters, a significant section of which had hewed to the right in the 2026 Assembly elections.

title: Kerala police are investigating Instagram and YouTube 'educational channels' that offer test-paper clues to lure anxious school students taking Onam mid-term examinations
author: G Anand
content_html:
The Kerala Police have initiated a preliminary probe into an array of online tutorial channels that seek to expand their subscription base and social media reach by exploiting the examination anxiety of school students and their parents. 

The General Education department on Sunday (August 16, 2026) petitioned State Police Chief Ravada A. Chandrasekhar for a detailed criminal inquiry into Instagram and YouTube channels which lure students by promising them definitive clues about the mid-term Onam test papers. 

An estimated 40 lakh school students from Class I to higher secondary are taking the Onam examinations, which will conclude on August 20.

Crime Branch inquiry

A senior police official said Mr. Chandrasekhar might initiate a Crime Branch inquiry and has sought a report from the Kerala Police Cyber Cell, including digital financial transactions. He said the police would also verify whether any errant teachers involved in the question-setting process were behind the racket. 

He said the police were also verifying whether the channels used the lure of examination clues and leaked question papers to dupe students and parents into sharing personal information, including e-mails, phone numbers, and credit card information, as part of a wider and illegal data-harvesting operation. 

Another official said the police would register cases if their inquiries reveal violations of the IT Act and infringement of the Public Examinations Act, which carry up to ten years’ imprisonment and significant fines. The police would also approach service providers to take down such fraudulent channels from social media. 

Officials said some online tuition channels under scrutiny claimed to have access to question papers and offered pointers on likely areas of the school syllabus students should focus on for good grades. They said the same channels also offered question papers prepared for model examinations, raising the spectre of widespread school examination fraud. 

Warns students, parents

Meanwhile, the department has warned students and parents to be vigilant about social media channels that entice them to subscribe by falsely promising advance clues about first-term question papers.

The government said the channels defeated the purpose of comprehensive school education by inducing students and parents to cut corners to achieve high grades in examinations. 

Earlier, several teachers’ organisations had flagged the peril posed by such so-called “educational channels.” Their false claims, the government said, could adversely affect school academics, teaching, and exam preparation.
